content.value_statement: Cross-border data projects can miss regulated scenarios, exemptions, filing thresholds, and recipient controls. This skill structures a China-focused assessment and produces practical compliance deliverables.
actual_capabilities: Identifies transfers, overseas access, foreign cloud use, remote employee access, and cross-border data exchanges.
Checks seven documented exemption categories before recommending a filing path.
Compares security assessment, standard contract, certification, and exemption routes.
Structures a data export risk self-assessment around purpose, scope, sensitivity, recipients, and foreign legal conditions.
Lists application materials, process steps, expected timelines, and recurring compliance tasks.
Drafts recipient-control requirements covering purpose limits, onward transfers, audits, termination, and deletion.
limitations: The knowledge base focuses on Chinese data export rules and does not fully analyze every destination jurisdiction.
The skill does not provide binding legal advice, regulator approval, certification, or filing services.
Thresholds, local regulator practices, and free-trade-zone lists can change after the knowledge base date.
Accurate conclusions require complete facts about data categories, volumes, operators, recipients, purposes, and transfer methods.

use_cases.title: Screen a New International Data Flow
use_cases.description: Map the transfer, classify the data, test exemptions, and identify the likely compliance route.

use_cases.title: Prepare Assessment or Filing Materials
use_cases.description: Create a structured checklist for self-assessment, security assessment, standard contract filing, or certification.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Overseas Recipient Controls
use_cases.description: Review recipient obligations, onward-transfer restrictions, security measures, audit rights, and deletion requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Transfer Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: List our potential data export scenarios from these facts: [facts]. Include overseas storage, remote access, foreign systems, employees, and business exchanges.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner inventory of cross-border data flows

prompt_templates.title: Check Exemptions and Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether this transfer may qualify for an exemption: [facts]. Then compare the remaining compliance routes and list missing facts.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Risk Self-Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a risk self-assessment outline for [transfer]. Cover data sensitivity, purpose, scope, recipient safeguards, foreign law, individual rights, and evidence needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced preparation for an internal legal review

prompt_templates.title: Design a Compliance Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an end-to-end compliance program for [organization]. Include governance, transfer records, route decisions, recipient controls, audits, renewals, and policy monitoring.

output_examples.input: A Chinese company stores ordinary customer account data on a foreign cloud service.
output: Potential transfer: direct transmission to an overseas server.
Required facts: operator status, individual count, sensitive information, important data, purpose, recipient, and transfer period.
Next step: test exemptions before comparing security assessment, standard contract, and certification.

output_examples.input: Overseas employees remotely access a system hosted in China.
output_examples.output: Treat overseas access as a potential data export. Inventory accessible fields, users, purposes, permissions, logging, and onward-transfer controls before selecting a route.

output_examples.input: Review an overseas recipient agreement for missing protections.
output_examples.output: Review purpose and scope limits, onward transfers, safeguards, individual rights, incident duties, audit rights, termination, deletion, and evidence retention.

best_practices: Provide verified facts about data types, volumes, sensitivity, operator status, recipients, destinations, purposes, and access methods.
Test every documented exemption before selecting a security assessment, standard contract, or certification route.
Confirm conclusions against current laws, official guidance, local regulator practice, and qualified legal counsel.
anti_patterns: Do not assume remote overseas access is outside data export rules.
Do not rely on headcount thresholds without checking sensitive information, important data, operator status, and cumulative periods.
Do not send personal records, credentials, contracts, or confidential datasets when anonymized facts are sufficient.

faq.question: Does overseas access to a system in China count as a data export?
faq.answer: It can. The skill treats overseas remote access as a transfer scenario that requires factual and legal review.

faq.question: Can the skill decide whether an exemption applies?
faq.answer: It can screen documented exemptions and identify missing facts. A qualified reviewer should confirm the final conclusion.

faq.question: Which compliance paths does the skill compare?
faq.answer: It compares security assessment, personal information standard contract filing, personal information protection certification, and exemption routes.

faq.question: Does the skill submit filings or issue legal opinions?
faq.answer: No. It prepares analyses and checklists but cannot file with regulators, certify compliance, or provide binding legal advice.

faq.question: What information produces the best assessment?
faq.answer: Provide data categories, volumes, sensitivity, operator status, recipients, destinations, purposes, transfer methods, retention, and safeguards.

faq.question: How should regulatory changes be handled?
faq.answer: Verify thresholds, official forms, validity periods, free-trade-zone lists, and local practices against current authoritative sources before acting.
